videos.author: 3Blue1Brown
videos.summary: The first chapter of 3Blue1Brown's Essence of Linear Algebra series, introducing vectors with animated geometric visuals. It begins a series that builds intuition for linear algebra from the basics.
videos.why: HN's go-to recommendation for learning linear algebra intuition, repeatedly credited with making concepts click and complementing textbooks.

videos.title: The spelled-out intro to neural networks and backpropagation: building micrograd
videos.author: Andrej Karpathy
videos.summary: Andrej Karpathy's first Neural Networks: Zero to Hero lecture, which builds micrograd, a tiny autograd engine, from scratch in Python. It explains backpropagation and neural network training step by step, assuming only basic Python and some high-school calculus.
videos.why: HN treats it as the best starting point for really understanding backprop and neural nets, because Karpathy explains the why with intuition and builds everything in code.

videos.title: AT&T Archives: Similiarities of Wave Behavior (Bonus Edition)
videos.author: AT&T Tech Channel
videos.summary: A Bell Labs film in which Dr. J.N. Shive uses a mechanical wave machine to demonstrate reflection, standing waves, resonance and impedance matching. He includes some equations but relies mostly on real-world examples a layperson can follow.
videos.why: HN repeatedly calls it the clearest introduction to waves and transmission-line behavior, better than modern explainers.

versions.title: 直观理解电路-波动的相似性(AT&T Archives Similiarities of Wave Behavior)

videos.title: How The Economic Machine Works by Ray Dalio
videos.author: Principles by Ray Dalio
videos.summary: Ray Dalio's 30-minute animated video explains how the economy works through credit, debt, interest rates, and short- and long-term cycles. It is based on his template for understanding the economy.
videos.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as the best layperson overview of debt, credit and economic cycles.

versions.title: How The Economic Machine Works 经济机器是怎样运行的 Principles by Ray Dalio

videos.title: RailsConf 2014 - All the Little Things by Sandi Metz
videos.author: Confreaks
videos.summary: Sandi Metz takes an ugly section of conditional code and refactors it into a few simple objects, bridging object-oriented theory and practice. The talk includes her take on the Gilded Rose refactoring kata and the idea that duplication is cheaper than the wrong abstraction.
videos.why: HN treats it as a top-tier programming talk for learning refactoring and for the wrong-abstraction principle, recommended repeatedly over a decade.

versions.title: 【搬运】所有的小事 RailsConf 2014 - All the Little Things by Sandi Metz

videos.title: But what is the Fourier Transform?  A visual introduction.
videos.author: 3Blue1Brown
videos.summary: 3Blue1Brown's animated visual introduction to the Fourier Transform, showing how a signal breaks into frequency components.
videos.why: HN's default recommendation for understanding the Fourier transform intuitively; many say it was the explanation that made it click.

versions.title: 【官方双语】形象展示傅里叶变换

videos.title: Around The Corner - How Differential Steering Works (1937)
videos.author: US Auto Industry
videos.summary: A 1937 GM-produced film explaining how the automobile differential lets wheels turn at different speeds around a corner. It uses clear animations and cutaway demonstrations to build the idea from first principles.
videos.why: Held up as a marvel of pedagogy and the best explanation of differentials, recommended again and again.

versions.title: 【熟肉】1937年雪弗兰公司科普片 “差速器的原理”

videos.title: "Simple Made Easy" - Rich Hickey (2011)
videos.author: Strange Loop Conference
videos.summary: Rich Hickey's Strange Loop 2011 keynote distinguishing 'simple' (not intertwined) from 'easy' (familiar or near at hand). It argues that software complexity comes from complecting things and that we should pick simple constructs.
videos.why: HN treats it as the canonical talk on software complexity, shared constantly and recommended to every programmer regardless of language.

versions.title: 容易 ≠ 简单 ("Simple Made Easy") - Rich Hickey (2011) | Strange Loop Conferen

videos.title: LEADERSHIP LAB: The Craft of Writing Effectively
videos.author: UChicago Social Sciences
videos.summary: Larry McEnerney of the University of Chicago Writing Program gives a graduate-student session on writing effectively. His core idea is that readers care about value to them, not the writer's thinking process.
videos.why: HN users repeatedly say it changed how they think about writing, calling it a masterclass useful far beyond academia.

versions.title: 芝加哥大学LEADERSHIP LAB_《有效写作的技巧|The Craft of Writing Effectively》中英字幕

videos.title: What the heck is the event loop anyway? | Philip Roberts | JSConf EU
videos.author: JSConf
videos.summary: Philip Roberts explains the JavaScript event loop, call stack, callbacks and asynchronous behavior with live visualizations using a tool he built. It demystifies terms like non-blocking and single-threaded.
videos.why: HN commenters repeatedly name it as the best explanation of the JS event loop and the first thing to watch before tackling async code.

versions.title: 【中文字幕】Philip Roberts：到底什么是Event Loop呢？（JSConf EU 2014）

videos.title: But what is a neural network? | Deep learning chapter 1
videos.author: 3Blue1Brown
videos.summary: 3Blue1Brown's first chapter on deep learning explains what neurons and layers are and the math underlying a basic neural network, using handwritten digit recognition with visual animations.
videos.why: HN treats it as the standard first stop for learning neural networks, praised for making the math intuitive.

videos.title: George Lakoff: Moral Politics
videos.author: University of California Television (UCTV)
videos.summary: Cognitive scientist George Lakoff lectures on how political debates are framed through language and metaphors tied to values, and on the moral worldviews behind progressive and conservative politics. It was given in 2005 at UC San Diego.
videos.why: HN commenters repeatedly say it changed how they hear political speech and recommend it for understanding why opponents are not simply stupid.

versions.title: 道德政治； 自由派和保守派如何思考-乔治•莱考夫 (George Lakoff）

videos.title: The Tragedy of systemd
videos.author: linux.conf.au
videos.summary: FreeBSD developer Benno Rice traces the history of init and bootstrap systems at linux.conf.au 2019 to explain why systemd was seen as necessary and why it provokes such strong reactions. He also discusses why change is scary.
videos.why: The most-recommended balanced take on systemd, from a BSD perspective, handed to anyone caught up in the systemd debate.

versions.title: 【人肉精翻】systemd的悲剧

videos.title: Rich Harris - Rethinking reactivity
videos.author: You Gotta Love Frontend
videos.summary: Svelte creator Rich Harris explains moving reactivity into the compiler and language rather than tracking state at runtime, with a history of spreadsheets as reactive systems and comparisons to React.
videos.why: The most recommended introduction to Svelte, credited with sparking its adoption.

versions.title: [Svelte] Rich Harris - Rethinking reactivity | 重新思考"响应式" - Svelte框架作者演讲

videos.title: SM64 - Watch for Rolling Rocks - 0.5x A Presses (Commentated) [OUTDATED]
videos.author: pannenkoek2012
videos.summary: Pannenkoek2012's commentated tool-assisted Super Mario 64 run collecting the Watch for Rolling Rocks star with half an A press, using parallel universes and QPU movement. The video is marked outdated in favor of a newer version.
videos.why: Held up as a legendary deep dive into game internals, explained lucidly and with humor, and a gateway to the channel.

versions.title: Watch for Rolling Rocks in 0.5x A presses

videos.title: 8-bit computer update
videos.author: Ben Eater
videos.summary: Ben Eater's short update announcing his plan to build another 8-bit computer from scratch on camera. It kicks off the breadboard computer series that became widely known.
videos.why: HN repeatedly recommends the series it launched as the best way to understand how a CPU works, praised for Eater's clear teaching.

versions.title: Building an 8-bit breadboard computer!

videos.title: Stanford's Sapolsky On Depression in U.S. (Full Lecture)
videos.author: Stanford
videos.summary: Stanford professor Robert Sapolsky lectures on depression as a real biological disease. He covers its biological and psychological causes, how it differs from ordinary sadness, and ideas such as learned helplessness. He ties these together into one account.
videos.why: HN returns to it repeatedly as the best single introduction to understanding clinical depression.

versions.title: Stanford's Sapolsky On Depression in U.S.

videos.title: The Continuity of Splines
videos.author: Freya Holmér
videos.summary: Freya Holmer's 74-minute video essay on splines, covering Bezier curves, B-splines, derivatives and the different levels of continuity (C0, C1, C2), built with custom animation tools. She notes she did not cover non-uniform splines.
videos.why: It is the go-to recommendation for anyone who wants to genuinely understand Bezier curves and splines, and commenters repeatedly call it one of the best programming-related educational videos.

versions.title: [ Freya Holmér]The Continuity of Splines（中英熟肉）

videos.title: Sugar: THE BITTER TRUTH
videos.author: University of California Television (UCTV)
videos.summary: Robert Lustig of UCSF lectures on the biochemistry of sugar, arguing that fructose and lack of fiber drive the obesity epidemic via insulin. It is the widely viewed 90-minute talk that popularized the anti-sugar case.
videos.why: The most-linked YouTube video on HN, recommended as an in-depth explanation of fructose metabolism.

versions.title: 糖：苦涩的真相  2009年7月31日

videos.title: Light Years Ahead | The 1969 Apollo Guidance Computer
videos.author: TNMoC
videos.summary: Robert Wills of TNMoC explains the Apollo Guidance Computer hardware and software, then walks through the Apollo 11 landing procedure step by step, including the 1202 alarms.
videos.why: HN calls it mandatory viewing on the AGC, praising the speaker's enthusiasm and the clear account of restartable, robust software design.

versions.title: 光年超前——1969年阿波罗登月球导航计算机

videos.title: Juice it or lose it - a talk by Martin Jonasson & Petri Purho
videos.author: grapefrukt
videos.summary: Martin Jonasson and Petri Purho take a bland Breakout clone and add layer after layer of 'juice' such as easing, particles, screen shake and sound until it feels alive. A live demo makes the effect of small feedback details obvious.
videos.why: The go-to recommendation on game feel and polish, cited by HN as one of the best talks for anyone making interactive things feel good.

videos.title: Lexical Scanning in Go - Rob Pike
videos.author: GoogleFOSSSydney
videos.summary: Rob Pike shows how the Go text/template lexer is built, using state functions, goroutines and channels. The talk was given at a Google Technology User Group in Sydney in 2011.
videos.why: HN returns to it for years as an elegant introduction to writing a lexer that is easy to follow even without a parsing background.

versions.title: Lexical Scanning In Go

videos.title: “Hello, world” from scratch on a 6502 — Part 1
videos.author: Ben Eater
videos.summary: Ben Eater starts a series building a working computer on breadboards around the 6502 microprocessor. In this first part he gets a 'hello world' running from scratch.
videos.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as the best hands-on way to understand how a CPU and a computer work from first principles.

versions.title: 【双语】如何使用后一块6502芯片打印出“hello world”-6502_Part_1

videos.title: What Happened to Horses Is Happening to Us
videos.author: CGP Grey
videos.summary: CGP Grey's video "Humans Need Not Apply" argues that automation will make a large part of the workforce economically obsolete, much as engines did for horses. It surveys robots and software replacing both physical and mental labor.
videos.why: HN has recommended it for a decade as the standard explainer on automation and unemployment, though skeptics later cite it as an example of overconfident predictions.

versions.title: 工作是人干的？不存在的！Humans Need Not Apply

videos.title: Bret Victor - Inventing on Principle
videos.author: Rui Oliveira
videos.summary: Bret Victor's talk at CUSEC 2012 in which he argues that creators need immediate feedback and should organize their work around a guiding principle. He demonstrates live-coding and animation tools that show results as you type, and describes his own principle that creators must see what they are making.
videos.why: It is HN's go-to recommendation for the case that programming environments should give instant feedback, and it appears in nearly every thread on live coding, visual programming or developer tools.

versions.title: 发明的准则 Bret Victor - Inventing on Principle
最伟大的界面设计演讲之一，送给AI时代迷茫的设计师 Bret Victor - Inventing on Principle
Bret Victor - 根据原则去发明 Inventing on Principle

videos.title: Bret Victor   The Future of Programming
videos.author: Joey Reid
videos.summary: Bret Victor's DBX 2013 talk, delivered in the guise of a 1973 IBM engineer with an overhead projector. It surveys forgotten ideas from 1960s and early 70s computing and warns against assuming you know what you're doing.
videos.why: HN treats it as a classic, near-mandatory talk on how programming tools and paradigms stagnated and which older ideas deserve revival.

versions.title: Bret Victor   The Future of Programming (2013)

videos.title: Jan Willem Nijman - Vlambeer - "The art of screenshake" at INDIGO Classes 2013
videos.author: Dutch Game Garden
videos.summary: Vlambeer's Jan Willem Nijman shows how to make an action game feel great by stacking small effects like screenshake, recoil and particles onto a basic shooter. It was presented at INDIGO Classes 2013.
videos.why: A perennial recommendation for anyone learning game feel and juice, praised for showing concrete steps that turn a bland prototype into a satisfying game.

versions.title: Jan Willem Nijman - Vlambeer - _The art of screenshake_ at INDIGO Classes 2013

videos.title: DON'T PANIC — Hans Rosling showing the facts about population
videos.author: Gapminder Foundation
videos.summary: Hans Rosling uses data and animated statistics to show how world population is changing, why birth rates fall as child survival and wealth rise, and why population is expected to peak around 11 billion. It also tackles common misconceptions about Africa and family planning.
videos.why: HN repeatedly recommends it to counter overpopulation alarm with data on falling birth rates.

versions.title: DON'T PANIC —世界人口学的真相-Hans Rosling（熟肉）

videos.title: Music Theory and White Supremacy
videos.author: Adam Neely
videos.summary: Adam Neely examines Phil Ewell's paper arguing Western music theory is framed by a white racial perspective. He covers North Indian theory, alternative frameworks, Schenker and responses to the paper.
videos.why: HN recommends it as the canonical video on how music theory is really the theory of one Western tradition, with the raga example.

versions.title: 【中文字幕】Music Theory and White Supremacy

videos.title: Overwatch Gameplay Architecture and Netcode
videos.author: GDC Festival of Gaming
videos.summary: Blizzard's Timothy Ford explains in this 2017 GDC session how Overwatch uses an Entity Component System architecture for layered gameplay. He also covers its server-authoritative netcode with client-side prediction and how they keep the game responsive and fair.
videos.why: HN treats it as the best real-world AAA example of ECS and game netcode, and cites it constantly in discussions of data-oriented design.

versions.title: 【青幻译制】GDC讲座系列之三 守望先锋的游戏架构和网络代码

videos.title: AlphaGo - The Movie | Full award-winning documentary
videos.author: Google DeepMind
videos.summary: Feature-length documentary following DeepMind's AlphaGo program as it prepares for and plays the 2016 match against Go champion Lee Sedol. It covers the team, the games, and the emotional reaction of the Go world to an AI beating a top human.
videos.why: HN commenters call it a moving, well-made human story about AI and Go that works for non-technical viewers and does not date.

versions.title: AlphaGo - The Movie | Full award-winning documentary

videos.title: But how does bitcoin actually work?
videos.author: 3Blue1Brown
videos.summary: 3Blue1Brown explains the math and mechanics behind Bitcoin visually: ledgers, digital signatures, proof of work and the blockchain, building up a decentralized payment system from first principles.
videos.why: The go-to recommended video for newcomers wanting a clear, visual explanation of how Bitcoin and blockchains work.

versions.title: 【官方双语】想知道比特币（和其他加密货币）的原理吗？

videos.title: Don't Talk to the Police
videos.author: Regent University School of Law
videos.summary: Regent Law professor James Duane gives startling reasons why people, even innocent ones, should always exercise their Fifth Amendment rights rather than talk to police. It is based on his article and book on the subject.
videos.why: HN treats it as the canonical video to link whenever talking to police or interrogations come up.

versions.title: Don't Talk to the Police

videos.title: TIMELAPSE OF THE FUTURE: A Journey to the End of Time (4K)
videos.author: melodysheep
videos.summary: A 29-minute cinematic timelapse by melodysheep that journeys trillions of years into the future, covering the death of the sun, the end of stars, proton decay, black hole evaporation and the fate of the cosmos.
videos.why: HN people recommend it as a stunning, mind-bending and existentially humbling view of deep time, and it appears on lists of favorite YouTube videos.

versions.title: 【4K】 时间之旅 —— 前往尽头

videos.title: Solving Problems the Clojure Way - Rafal Dittwald
videos.author: Clojure/north
videos.summary: Rafal Dittwald's Clojure/north talk shows how to move from writing Java-style code in Clojure to thinking in data-driven, functional terms. He walks through a JavaScript example, refactoring imperative code step by step into a functional core.
videos.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as a fantastic demonstration of procedural, OOP and FP approaches to the same problem, and of functional core and imperative shell.

versions.title: Solving Problems the Clojure Way - Rafal Dittwald

videos.title: "Uncle" Bob Martin - "The Future of Programming"

videos.summary: Robert C. Martin (Uncle Bob) traces the history of software from 1948 to today, looking at the problems programmers faced, how they were solved, and what mistakes the profession made. He then projects where the field is going, including professionalism and regulation.
videos.why: HN recommends it as an engaging overview of programming history and an argument for professional standards, citing the agile manifesto section and the claim that software has advanced little since the 1950s.

versions.title: Uncle Bob Martin-The Future of Programming

videos.title: Effective Programs - 10 Years of Clojure - Rich Hickey
videos.author: ClojureTV
videos.summary: Rich Hickey's talk at Clojure's tenth anniversary on the kind of programs Clojure is designed for. He argues for situated programs that deal with changing requirements, and for dynamic typing and data over static types.
videos.why: HN's go-to link in typing debates and for talk lists, and several call it their favorite programming talk even for non-Clojure users.

versions.title: Effective Programs - 10 Years of Clojure - Rich Hickey-2V1FtfBDsLU

videos.title: Richard Sutton – Father of RL thinks LLMs are a dead end
videos.author: Dwarkesh Patel
videos.summary: Dwarkesh Patel interviews Richard Sutton, reinforcement learning pioneer, Turing Award winner and author of The Bitter Lesson. Sutton argues LLMs are a dead end because they cannot learn on the job, and that continual learning from experience will require a new architecture.
videos.why: HN commenters cite it as the serious skeptic's case against LLMs reaching general intelligence, usually in debates about whether scaling is enough.

versions.title: Richard Sutton – Father of RL thinks LLMs are a dead end

videos.title: Let's prototype a JavaScript JIT compiler!
videos.author: Andreas Kling
videos.summary: Andreas Kling live-codes a prototype JavaScript JIT compiler for the LibJS engine used in SerenityOS and Ladybird. He builds a standalone bytecode VM, a simple interpreter, and then a simple JIT in about 80 minutes.
videos.why: HN commenters cite it as a concrete example of how a skilled developer uses Copilot, mostly as fancy autocomplete for codebase-specific work.

versions.title: Let's prototype a JavaScript JIT compiler! |  Andreas Kling

videos.title: Richard Stallman Free software Song
videos.author: BeatStock
videos.summary: A short clip of Richard Stallman singing the free software song, recorded during a visit to Ecuador.
videos.why: HN posts it as a lighthearted joke link in free software and licensing threads.

versions.title: Richard Stallman Free software Song

videos.title: An Observation on Generalization
videos.author: Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing
videos.summary: Ilya Sutskever gives a Simons Institute talk on why neural networks generalize, framing learning as finding short descriptions, like compression. It was part of the Large Language Models and Transformers program.
videos.why: Cited in discussions of learning as compression and of why neural networks generalize.

versions.title: 【中英精校】An Observation on Generalization

videos.title: The Inside Story of ChatGPT’s Astonishing Potential | Greg Brockman | TED
videos.author: TED
videos.summary: OpenAI cofounder Greg Brockman explains the design principles behind ChatGPT and demos unreleased plug-ins at TED 2023. In the follow-up, TED head Chris Anderson presses him on the timeline of development and the risks of releasing such a tool.
videos.why: HN commenters cite it as a primary source for Brockman's views, such as moving fast to reduce risk, and for capability anecdotes like GPT-4's arithmetic.

versions.title: The Inside Story of ChatGPT’s Astonishing Potential | Greg Brockman | TED

videos.title: Vibe Coding Is The Future
videos.author: Y Combinator
videos.summary: A Y Combinator video on vibe coding, the term Andrej Karpathy coined for letting LLMs write code. It reports what YC founders say about debugging, models and how much of their code is AI-written.
videos.why: HN mostly cites it critically, as a source for the claim that much of YC code is AI-written and as an example of insiders promoting vibe coding.

versions.title: 《Vibe Coding Is The Future》- Y Combintor

videos.title: Sam Altman: OpenAI CEO on GPT-4, ChatGPT, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #367
videos.author: Lex Fridman
videos.summary: Lex Fridman's long interview with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman about GPT-4, ChatGPT, and the future of AI. Topics include models as reasoning engines, AI risk, and consciousness.
videos.why: HN mostly cites it for specific Altman quotes, such as models as reasoning engines rather than databases, while many commenters found the interview shallow or insincere.

versions.title: Sam Altman: OpenAI CEO on GPT-4, ChatGPT, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman

videos.title: WWDC 2024 — June 10 | Apple
videos.author: Apple
videos.summary: Apple's WWDC 2024 keynote introducing Apple Intelligence along with iOS 18, iPadOS 18, macOS Sequoia, watchOS 11 and visionOS 2.
videos.why: HN links to specific segments of the keynote to back up claims about features like Passwords, Math Notes and the ChatGPT handoff.

versions.title: WWDC 2024 — June 10  Apple【1440P】

videos.title: Interview with Senior Rust Developer
videos.author: Kai Lentit
videos.summary: A short comedy sketch by Kai Lentit lampooning an interview with a 'senior Rust developer' and Rust community stereotypes.
videos.why: HN posts it as a humorous aside in Rust debates, often to poke fun at Rust evangelism and community culture.

versions.title: Interview with Senior Rust Developer in 2023

videos.title: Andrej Karpathy — “We’re summoning ghosts, not building animals”
videos.author: Dwarkesh Patel
videos.summary: Dwarkesh Patel interviews Andrej Karpathy on why reinforcement learning is flawed, why AGI may blend into steady GDP growth, why self-driving took so long, and the future of education. The conversation runs about two and a half hours.
videos.why: Mostly cited as a source for Karpathy's views on agents, AGI timelines and LLMs, rather than recommended outright.

versions.title: Andrej Karpathy — “We’re summoning ghosts, not building animals”

videos.title: Keynote (Google I/O '18)
videos.author: Google for Developers
videos.summary: The Google I/O 2018 keynote led by Sundar Pichai, covering Google's product and platform announcements. Highlights included AI features such as smart replies and the Assistant.
videos.why: Referenced mostly as the primary source for what Google announced, such as AI features, rather than recommended on its own merits.

versions.title: Google IO 2018 开发者大会Keynote 官方版 (Google I/O '18)

videos.title: I Interviewed The Creator Of LLVM, Clang, Swift, and Mojo
videos.author: The PrimeTime
videos.summary: ThePrimeagen interviews Chris Lattner, creator of LLVM, Clang, Swift and Mojo, with TJ DeVries, in a long live-streamed conversation. They discuss language design and Lattner's experience building Swift.
videos.why: Cited in Swift discussions for Lattner's account of Swift becoming complex too fast under pressure from Apple's needs.

versions.title: I Interviewed The Creator Of LLVM, Clang, Swift, and Mojo | Primeagen
